title: Prime avoidance
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $J\subset R$ an ideal and $I_1,\dots,I_r\subset R$ ($r\ge1$) ideals all but at most two of which are prime ideals. If $J\not\subset I_i$ for $i=1,\dots,r$, then there is $x\in J$ with $x\notin I_i$ for all $i$. Equivalently: if $J\subseteq I_1\cup\dots\cup I_r$ then $J\subseteq I_i$ for some $i$.

mathlib_searches.query: prime avoidance: an ideal contained in a finite union of prime ideals is contained in one of them
